question: Does tutoring-bot feedback improve short-term quiz scores in the summarized studies, and for whom?
required_claim: Improvement is reported for low-prior-knowledge students; one study finds no average effect.

passages.text: Campus Wi-Fi latency was measured across three dormitories during exam week. Median latency remained under 40 ms.
Study A (RCT, n=120) found that immediate tutoring-bot feedback raised short-term quiz scores for students with low prior knowledge (standardized effect ≈ 0.35).
Library seating capacity increased by 15% after renovation. Student satisfaction with noise levels was unchanged.
A survey of teaching assistants reported higher workload when courses adopted weekly online quizzes.
Study B (survey, n=80) reported no significant average difference in quiz scores between tutoring-bot and static-answer conditions.
The registrar noted that course withdrawal rates fell slightly after mid-semester advising emails.
An HCI pilot study redesigned the bot interface icons; usability scores improved, but learning outcomes were not measured.
